correctness.rationale: Every hypothesis and objective is explicitly defined. The Walsh radial spectrum gives sharp spectral lower bound, small-d interpolation, and construction. Full-eigenspace saturation forces global uniqueness for d<=4. Degree-one and parity-mode saturation force zero holding and per-coordinate flip marginal for every optimizer with d>=4; explicit translation-invariant perturbations preserve all active modes and remain under the strict interior spectral bounds for d>=5. This proves affine dimension C(d,2)-1 for translation-invariant optima, without claiming to classify vertex-dependent optimizer faces. The standalone package verifier executed 228683 exact arithmetic assertions, covering finite but not infinite dimensions.

value.rationale: Characterizing the entire optimal-support rigidity transition is a natural question for fastest-mixing Markov-chain design. It provides a sharp dimension threshold between uniquely determined weights and a continuously flexible optimal face, plus mandatory local marginal allocations even when many optimal implementations exist. The fact is not just the known edge-transitive optimal value: it describes degrees of freedom for secondary implementation constraints.
